title: Derive the settled-entry count in RuleCases C-001 instead of pinning '7 settled'
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C-001 asserts the summary line without a hard-coded settled count: missing
C-001 stays green as later slices append settled entries: missing
C-001 still fails if parity output is wrong, so it keeps its bite: partial
Throwaway build-time probe versus a permanent negative test of C-001's bite: a permanent test survives but adds fixture machinery to a suite no gate runs.
Lifting C-007's inline rule-count expression into a shared function versus duplicating it: sharing is one source but touches a green case.

Adding an architecture rule for a one-file test-bookkeeping fix versus relying on the derived count alone: the rule is the only enforcement anyone will see, given O-005, but it adds one more settled entry.
Keeping 11, 15 and 27 as literals versus deriving all four numbers: literals cost a deliberate hand edit only when the parity tool itself changes.
Names and placement of ExpectedSettled and the rule-count function within RuleCases.ps1.
